summary:
Towards Robust Mathematical Reasoning - Thang Luong, Dawsen Hwang, Hoang H. Nguyen, Golnaz Ghiasi, Yuri Chervonyi, Insuk Seo, Junsu Kim, Garrett Bingham, Jonathan Lee, Swaroop Mishra, Alex Zhai, Clara Huiyi Hu, Henryk Michalewski, Jimin Kim, Jeonghyun Ahn, Junhwi Bae, Xingyou Song, Trieu H. Trinh, Quoc V. Le, Junehyuk Jung, 2025

The paper targets a benchmark-design failure mode in mathematical reasoning evaluation: widely used math benchmarks are either saturated, too short-answer-centric, or insufficiently sensitive to proof quality, making them poor optimization targets for frontier reasoning models. It introduces IMO-Bench, a benchmark suite explicitly calibrated to International Mathematical Olympiad difficulty and vetted by expert mathematicians. The suite is split into IMO-AnswerBench, a 400-problem set of diverse Olympiad-style questions with verifiable short answers, and IMO-Proof Bench, a proof-generation benchmark spanning basic and advanced IMO-level problems with detailed grading rubrics intended to support automatic assessment of long-form proofs. The technical objective is not merely harder evaluation, but robust measurement of both answer correctness and proof-writing competence under expert-aligned standards.

Concretely, the work builds three artifacts: the IMO-Bench evaluation suite, Gemini-based proof autograders, and IMO-GradingBench, a dataset of 1000 human proof gradings for calibrating and studying automatic grading quality. The reported results show Gemini Deep Think reaching 80.0 percent on IMO-AnswerBench and 65.7 percent on the advanced split of IMO-Proof Bench, exceeding the best non-Gemini baselines by 6.9 and 42.4 percentage points respectively. The paper further claims that the Gemini reasoning-based autograders correlate well with human judgments, positioning grading-model quality itself as a measurable research target rather than an ad hoc evaluation convenience. In effect, the contribution is an evaluation framework that shifts mathematical reasoning research from short-answer accuracy toward robust, rubric-grounded assessment of Olympiad-level proof synthesis. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01846))
